title: SS03 6-round AES-128 Consistent-pattern key recovery

target.description: Standard128-bit Rijndael block and128-bit key; 6 rounds, finalMC omitted. Recover full terminal round key, use backward key expansion and consistency checks to obtain the complete master key.

success.description: The exact6-round data/time endpoint has no reported numerical end-to-end master-key success. Correct-key retention by a necessary deterministic pattern is separate from uniqueness and expected work. Source accidental-pattern probabilities are heuristic wrong-key filters, not false-negative or recovery rates. The second structure validates proposed key components; the final key-schedule check is not given a numerical success rate. The existing S-box conversion conflict remains.

review.scope: Re-read PDF5–14 Sections3.2 and4.1–4.4. Five-round Section4.3 explicitly invokes Section4.2's final four-difference false-key argument; a conservative all2^128-key union bound gives conditional complete-output correctness under that source heuristic, without using the disputed2^16 worst-case candidate cap. Six rounds still lacks an assembled false-output distribution. Neither result gets a hard native-work-cap guarantee. Preserve expected-versus-worst-case and S-box conversion conflicts and both original components per endpoint.

components.description: Section4.4: a correct key satisfies the required consistent-difference/balanced pattern and is not rejected by that necessary-condition test, assuming exhaustive candidate enumeration. This does not prove unique identification or the stated finite work budget.
PDF14 Section4.4 Checking the Key Components: source1/2^64 for an erroneous candidate to satisfy Pattern5 on the second data set. This is not a final master-key recovery probability.
